$comment: Contract-conformance declarations. Every entry here is a declared-unconsumed
surface: a capability that exists, that no client reaches, and that is
deliberately left that way. It must match reality exactly -- a missing entry
is an undeclared finding and an entry that is no longer true is a stale one,
and both fail a -strict run. See docs/prds/contract-conformance-audit.md.
Managed by tools/contractaudit. Reasons state the consequence, not 'TODO':
this file is the only place the debt is legible.

StateStoreService/ListCaptures.reason: Superseded by StreamCaptures. The remote adapter's ListCaptures method (staterpc/client.go) calls StreamCaptures, not this unary RPC, so no production client reaches it. The server keeps it implemented as a compatibility surface for callers of the raw proto.

StateStoreService/ListUndispatchedCaptur.reason: Superseded by StreamUndispatchedCaptures, on the same terms as ListCaptures: the remote adapter's ListUndispatchedCaptures calls the streaming variant, leaving this unary RPC reachable only through the raw proto.

blindSpots.reason: A path counts as a consumer only when it is the first argument of a call in code. The function need not be named -- naming it broke on rename, when matching `req|fetch` reported 16 live routes as unconsumed after the dashboard's helper became `request(` -- but a bare constant, a dead array, an object property, or a commented-out call must not count, because crediting any quoted literal makes the surface pass on a file that issues no requests at all. Limits: a path passed as any argument other than the first is not seen (accepting a comma would start crediting array elements); a request inside a template-literal interpolation is not seen; a path built from a bare /api fragment is reported as unparsable; and a route is credited to every HTTP verb, so a route whose specific verb has no caller reads as consumed. Routes whose consumer is outside the dashboard (the asset mount, the health probes, the capture-intake webhook) are excluded from this surface by design: they have different consumers and are not part of the dashboard API contract.

Consumption is derived by scanning adapter bodies for calls through the generated client. An RPC reached only through runtime-loaded code (Yaegi) or reflection would read as unconsumed. No such path exists today.
As above. Note that gatewayrpc is served by archie-gateway and consumed by archied and archie-ui; a consumer living outside this repository would be invisible here.
